short: The best-armed and best-armoured tank of its day, and among the slowest.
full:
Chieftain entered British service in 1966 carrying the 120 mm L11 rifled gun with separate bagged charges, and a well-sloped glacis made possible by a driver who lay back almost flat to steer. On paper, and largely in fact, it had more armour and more gun than any contemporary. The trade was mobility: the Leyland L60 multi-fuel engine was underpowered and so unreliable that availability rates in Germany became a political embarrassment.

Britain never fired one in anger. Its export customers did. Iran took delivery of around 700 and used them heavily against Iraq from 1980, losing many in the fighting around Khorramshahr and Susangerd. Kuwaiti Chieftains fought the Iraqi invasion in August 1990 and again on the way out. Challenger 1 began to replace it in British armoured regiments from 1983, and the last Chieftain gun tanks left front-line British service in 1995.
